en: The Introduction to the Chapter on the Puzzling Questions;
The Section on the Qualities of a Lay Follower.
6. Upāsakaguṇa Thera, having accepted with the words “Very well,” elucidated the ten qualities of a lay follower:
“Great King, these ten are the qualities of a lay follower.”

Which ten? Here, Great King, a lay follower shares in the same joys and sorrows as the Saṅgha; he has the Dhamma as his authority; he delights in sharing according to his ability; seeing the decline of the Victor’s teaching, he strives for its increase. He possesses right view;
being free from superstitious omens and charms, he does not point to another teacher even for the sake of his life;
his bodily and verbal conduct are guarded; he delights in harmony and rejoices in harmony; and he is free from envy.
And he does not conduct himself in the Dispensation out of hypocrisy; he has gone for refuge to the Buddha, he has gone for refuge to the Dhamma, he has gone for refuge to the Saṅgha.
These, O Great King, are the ten qualities of a lay follower, and all these qualities are found in you. You—
"It is fitting, appropriate, suitable, and proper for you that, seeing the decline of the Victor’s teaching, you desire its increase.
I grant you leave; ask me whatever you wish.
The introductory discourse on the beginning of the Meṇḍaka questions is concluded.
